title: Clendon Thomas: 1957 Consensus All-American Halfback at OU
question: Which Oklahoma halfback led the nation in scoring in 1956 and became a College Football Hall of Famer?
answer: Clendon Thomas, who played for Oklahoma from 1955 to 1957, led the nation in scoring in 1956 with 18 touchdowns and was a consensus All-American in 1957. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2011.
summary: Clendon Thomas led the nation in scoring in 1956, became a consensus All-American in 1957, helped OU win 47 straight, and later reached the Pro Bowl.
body: Clendon Thomas was a lean Oklahoma City halfback who played for Bud Wilkinson at Oklahoma from 1955 through 1957, during the years when the Sooners simply did not lose. The College Football Hall of Fame lists his college record at 31-1 and notes that he was part of the undefeated 1955 and 1956 national championship teams.

His junior season was his loudest. In 1956 he led the nation in scoring with 18 touchdowns and earned second-team All-America honors. He was also a first-team all-conference pick that year, and his running never dipped below 6.3 yards per carry in any of his three seasons.

As a senior in 1957 he became a consensus All-American and finished ninth in the Heisman Trophy voting, won that year by Texas A&M's John David Crow. Over his career he piled up 2,118 rushing yards and 3,209 all-purpose yards, and he scored 36 touchdowns on just 355 touches, roughly once every ten times he handled the ball.
He was a member of the teams that ran the 47-game winning streak, still the longest in major college history. Thomas was also a fine defender, which pointed him toward his pro future.

The Los Angeles Rams picked him in the second round of the 1958 NFL draft as a defensive back. He played 11 seasons with the Rams and the Pittsburgh Steelers, collecting 27 interceptions and 10 fumble recoveries, and he made the Pro Bowl after the 1963 season. The College Football Hall of Fame inducted him in 2011.
